presentation.label: SCENE MORPH
presentation.summary: Lock MIDI track parameters to scenes and morph them with the crossfader.
presentation.overview: MIDISC2.0 adds MIDI scene locks and crossfader morphing, with pre-trig operation, pattern/Part boundary timing, active-lock preservation, CC-before-note ordering and sequencer ACT Part sync. This candidate reconstructs the actual author release, with standalone MAIN parity verified; publication remains pending.
highlights: Scene A/B locks on MIDI tracks
Crossfader morphing with step parameter locks
Standalone MIDISC2.0: pre-trig scenes and pattern/Part sync
usage: Hold Scene A or B while editing an enabled MIDI parameter to create a scene lock.
Release the scene key and sweep the crossfader between assigned scenes.
The tutorial uses CC1 assigned to controller 74, base 0 and scene-held value 64.

limitations: Candidate outside public catalog and native discovery; not downloadable.
The fixed 2.0 patch regions collide with current remixer allocations; mixed configurations are unsupported.
Complete control qualification, worst-case cycles and exact memory accounting remain pending; standalone full update packaging parity passed.
The hardware report is owner-accepted functional evidence, with unspecified model/workload/timing.

access.location: MIDI track parameter pages: hold SCENE A or SCENE B and edit an enabled parameter; the example uses MIDI CTRL 1.
steps: Press MIDI to enter MIDI mode and select a track with its TRACK key.
For an external receiver, open MIDI NOTE SETUP with FUNC + SRC, choose CHAN with encoder A and press YES to confirm. The capture fixture has no connected receiver and leaves CHAN off.
For the illustrated CC example, hold FUNC and press FX1 to open MIDI CTRL 1 SETUP. Assign controller 74 to CC1 with encoder C and press YES to confirm.
Press FX1 to return to MIDI CTRL 1. Hold FUNC and press encoder C to enable CC1; its default OFF state cannot be edited as a normal active control.

Hold SCENE A or SCENE B and press a TRIG key to assign a scene to that side. Keep the scene key held and turn encoder C to set its CC1 scene lock. The pictured example locks CC1 to 64 while the base value is 0.
Release the scene key. Move the crossfader to morph the assigned scenes. Other supported MIDI parameter pages use the same hold-and-edit pattern.
